name: Governed symptom follow-up on a reading

parameters.content:
## Governed symptom follow-up on a reading

**Self-hosted n8n only.** This template uses the AnyBio Govern community node (`n8n-nodes-anybio`). Community nodes are not available on n8n Cloud until they are verified.

### Who's it for
Care teams and digital health builders running remote monitoring who want an AI to draft patient check-ins, with a policy check before any message reaches a patient.

### How it works
A blood pressure reading arrives by webhook. AnyBio Govern records the AI-identity disclosure, an OpenAI model drafts a symptom check-in, and AnyBio Govern evaluates the draft under your Govern policy:
- **Deliver**: the draft is allowed; Twilio sends it.
- **Show Hold Text**: the draft is stopped and a holding line is owed; Twilio sends your holding line, never the draft.
- **Send Nothing**: nothing is owed (an opt-out, missing consent, the message cap) or AnyBio could not be reached. Nothing goes to the patient.

Every branch reports the outcome, so the record reads proposed, decided, delivered.

### How to set up
1. Install the community node: **Settings > Community nodes > Install**, enter `n8n-nodes-anybio`.
2. Create three credentials: **AnyBio Govern API** (a sandbox application key, Environment set to Sandbox) for Record Disclosure, AnyBio Govern, Report Delivered and Report Not Sent; **OpenAI** for Chat Model; **Twilio** for Send SMS.
3. Fill in **Your settings**.
4. Click **Execute workflow** to run the pinned sample reading, or POST the same JSON to the test URL on **Reading In**.

### Requirements
- Self-hosted n8n with community nodes enabled
- An AnyBio Govern application key (sandbox for testing)
- An OpenAI API key
- A Twilio account with an SMS-capable number

### How to customize the workflow
- Edit **Your settings**: holding line, disclosure text, channel, audience, sender number, chat model.
- Change the prompt in **Draft Follow-up**, or swap in another chat model.
- Keep **Send Nothing** connected only to the outcome report.

Test with synthetic data only: the sample uses fictional 555-01xx numbers and synthetic IDs.

### 1. The reading comes in

POST a JSON body shaped like the pinned test data. **Your settings** holds the values you change:

```json
{
  "conversationId": "synthetic-conv-001",
  "readingId": "synthetic-reading-001",
  "patientRef": "synthetic-patient-001",
  "phone": "+12025550142",
  "reading": { "systolic": 162, "diastolic": 98 }
}
```

`readingId` becomes the AnyBio Govern node's turn ID, so a re-delivered reading replays the stored decision instead of drafting a second message.

### 2. Disclosure, then the draft

Every patient-audience turn needs the AI-identity disclosure on record for the conversation, or Govern holds it. This template assumes the program's enrollment message showed the disclosure below and records it (once per conversation; a repeat returns the same evidence).

Swap the chat model for your own. The prompt never gives medication instructions, and Govern enforces that anyway.

### 3. Only Deliver and Show Hold Text reach the SMS node

SMS is outbound, so a hold shows text only when AnyBio says a holding line is owed, and at most once per decision. **Send Nothing** is connected only to the outcome report: never connect anything that messages the patient to it.

The Hold Message on AnyBio Govern is your holding line: fixed text your clinical owner wrote in advance, never model-written.

assignments.name: holdMessage
assignments.value: Thanks for your reading. A nurse from your care team will reply within one business day. If you have chest pain or trouble breathing, call 911 now.

assignments.name: disclosureText
assignments.value: Your Care Program: messages in this conversation are written by an automated assistant. Your care team reviews anything it is unsure about. Reply STOP to opt out.

parameters.text: =You are drafting one SMS for a remote blood pressure monitoring program. The patient's latest reading was {{ $('Reading In').item.json.body.reading.systolic }}/{{ $('Reading In').item.json.body.reading.diastolic }} mmHg. Ask how they are feeling and whether they have a headache, chest pain, shortness of breath or vision changes, and tell them their care team will see their answer. Do not give medication or dosing instructions. Plain text, under 300 characters.
